fichas.title: Zoo Enclosures: Design Aspects
fichas.summary: Enclosures should evoke an appropriate natural habitat, bring visitors physically and emotionally close to animals, and encourage exploration and lingering. Observation should be comfortable and unobstructed, while allowing animals to withdraw from view. Keeper access, signage, and sufficient information are also required.
spaces: Keeper access roads and care areas
uses: Allow animals to withdraw from view
Provide keeper access and animal handling

fichas.title: Zoo Enclosures: Barriers
fichas.summary: Water moats, protective glass, and fences or walls can separate visitors from animals. Moats should have a natural appearance, but water quality and winter freezing require consideration. Glass can give visitors an impression of direct contact while limiting transmission of infection; bars are discouraged in modern zoos.
